title: Forearm swelling - investigation
clarityIssues: The examination does not explicitly locate the firm swelling relative to subcutis, fascia or tendon; pain limiting wrist movement makes that distinction relevant.
fairness: Ultrasonography is a reasonable first investigation, but the visible findings establish superficial localization less clearly than the explanation assumes. No confident clinical error is established.
The response discrepancy can require two steps: identify a persistent focal problem despite improving skin inflammation, then select its initial anatomical assessment.
The subsequent ultrasound update is coherent and must remain hidden until this choice is answered.
suggestions: Add a concise observed examination finding establishing the superficial location; do not announce an abscess diagnosis.
Keep the explanation conditional until imaging establishes a collection. Strengthen the competing investigations using actual patient-specific reasons.

Report-wide scope: all 26 after-version nodes reviewed offline, including preceding visible feedback. Five kept records, 34 proposed retirement records, seven unkeyed candidates and the existing withheld teaching point were noted, not re-reviewed. Verdicts are editorial judgments, not fresh source verification or clinical sign-off.

title: Forearm swelling - drainage
fairness: Incision and drainage is the defensible best offered treatment for the symptomatic superficial collection. Aspiration and complete excision are weak competitors here.
Classic cavity recognition followed by routine drainage is one familiar management rule. Improving redness does not materially distinguish the offered procedures.
The update follows the investigation coherently and stands alone. Prior feedback has already emphasized the unresolved collection.
suggestions: Use a supported source-control boundary where an observed finding changes procedure or setting, with credible alternatives.
If this remains basic abscess treatment, obtain explicit acceptance of a foundational role rather than describing it as difficult.

title: Recurrent back swelling - investigation

cues.why: The stem describes a skin/subcutaneous focus; the spine-targeted option advertises a target mismatch.
With only chest/spine alternatives, the regional soft-tissue investigation can be selected by tissue-category matching without reasoning about recurrence.

fairness: Ultrasonography is a reasonable best offered test for a recurrent superficial lesion after a splinter injury. No confident clinical inaccuracy is identified.
The test can be selected simply because the lesion is superficial; the splinter and recurrence do not earn an independent consequential step.
The later foreign-body finding is coherent and not required here.
suggestions: Compare investigations that plausibly evaluate the same target.
Make the penetrating injury or a documented initial-assessment limitation change the investigation, rather than using unrelated chest/spine workup as padding.

title: Recurrent back swelling - source control
clarityIssues: Excision of overlying skin and subcutis does not define its boundaries or whether it removes the imaged structure; it can overlap the key.

cues.why: Foreign-material removal is a straightforward lay match, reinforced by the preceding explanation.

cues.phrase: a local anatomical assessment for fluid and retained material
cues.why: The preceding explanation rehearses the object sought; the next task largely asks the learner to remove that object.

fairness: Removal of a retained nidus with appropriate cavity management is sound. The alternative excision is not clearly distinct enough to exclude accomplishing the same goal.
The ultrasound update is coherent and independently interpretable, but this sequence reduces to recognition followed by removal.
suggestions: Specify each procedure target and extent so alternatives do not implicitly include the same source control.
Compare credible approaches whose ranking depends on supported anatomical findings, rather than broad excessive excision.

title: Thigh redness - initial treatment
clarityIssues: A nonpurulent-cellulitis antimicrobial course names a pathway rather than an actual medicine or sufficiently specific regimen.

cues.why: Directly eliminates the drainage choice in this otherwise uncomplicated presentation.
Directly opposes the fascial-exploration alternative; the two explicit exclusions leave the only medication option.
The key supplies a diagnostic category while the alternatives name concrete procedures, creating category and specificity asymmetry.

fairness: The intended nonpurulent infection pathway is reasonable. No confidently wrong clinical key is identified.
The alternative operations have no credible supporting findings; the choices do not test a consequential second inference.
A later cavity is a coherent interval change, not a contradiction of the original scan.
suggestions: Name an actual treatment in every option and provide the necessary facts to distinguish credible current-stage plans.
Keep necessary collection exclusion, but change the comparison so it does not eliminate every alternative.

title: Thigh redness - new collection
fairness: The new symptomatic superficial collection supports incision and drainage despite the earlier negative scan. Chronology is clear and the update stands alone.
The new cavity already supplies the routine drainage indication. The earlier negative study does not distinguish any offered procedure.
Aspiration and broad skin/subcutis excision are weak alternatives; no confident clinical error in the key is identified.
suggestions: Make the earlier/current discrepancy change a plausible management decision instead of repeating the forearm drainage question.
Retain current observations and chronology; replace weak competitors or propose merging the redundant objective.

title: Foot admission review - setting and source control
fairness: The deep plantar cavity between tendons and worsening function support hospital-capable drainage/debridement with systemic treatment. Improving redness, no fever and a susceptible surface isolate do not establish source control.
The balanced four-option matrix requires source-control selection and setting selection. Each component appears twice, so component-frequency convergence does not identify the key.
The historical hospital frame identifies whose decision is reviewed but does not itself establish that admission was appropriate; anatomy must justify the plan.
The operative-specimen follow-up is coherent. This offline editorial PASS is not clinical approval.

title: Foot admission review - operative specimen
clarityIssues: The cavity was drained, but the task asks what to collect at the operation. Clarify that the decision occurs during the procedure before completion.

cues.phrase: The present decision is the specimen for soft-tissue pathogen identification; bone involvement has not been demonstrated.
cues.why: This authorial instruction names the target and suppresses bone sampling, repeating the preceding observation.

cues.phrase: A prior swab was taken from fluid on the external dressing.
cues.why: An obviously remote sample steers toward operative-site tissue when alternatives are surface swab and bone.

fairness: Aseptic sampling of infected soft tissue is best among the choices. Absence of visible bone involvement does not itself exclude osteomyelitis; keep the task about the drained soft-tissue infection.
The operative findings follow coherently, but this is target-to-specimen matching, not two consequential steps.
suggestions: Replace the meta-instruction with a concise operative observation and clear sampling time.
Compare relevant specimens with a meaningful collection/provenance difference instead of a bone option excluded by the task.

title: Persistent toe ulcer - further imaging

cues.phrase: Radiographs show no definite cortical destruction
cues.why: Radiography is offered again without an interval or protocol difference; it reads as a disposable completed-test foil.
This makes surface swab a target mismatch, leaving MRI after discounting the completed radiographs.

fairness: MRI is a reasonable best next test when initial clinical, radiographic and laboratory assessment leaves bone involvement uncertain.
This is a standard next-test rule with two weak alternatives; imperfect probing and mildly elevated markers do not create a competing pathway.
The later MRI update is coherent and remains unavailable here.
suggestions: Replace the swab and unexplained repeat radiograph with credible same-stage investigations or plans.
If repeat radiography remains, supply an actual reason it might help and sufficient chronology/protocol detail to rank it; invent no interval.

title: Persistent toe ulcer - bone sampling
clarityIssues: The task does not explicitly distinguish microbiology, histology or both; the explanation discusses compartment and contamination without clarifying the specimen purpose.

cues.phrase: Bone obtained aseptically through intact skin
cues.why: Only the key advertises asepsis and avoidance of the ulcer; both alternatives visibly sample the ulcer, giving the key a procedural-quality advantage.

fairness: Aseptic bone sampling is a defensible best offered specimen when osteomyelitis is the treatment target. Abnormal marrow is not microbiological proof.
The update supplies the suspected compartment; selecting that compartment is one familiar rule rather than two consequential decisions.
The MRI follows the workup coherently and the update supplies the relevant new findings independently.
suggestions: State the specimen purpose and give collection methods in comparably neutral detail.
Create a genuine sampling-provenance or diagnostic-discordance problem with credible competitors rather than aseptic bone versus surface material.

title: Foot salvage review - coordinated consultation

cues.why: The key is the only urgent, comprehensive response; both alternatives advertise delay despite deep infection and poor perfusion.
Delayed vascular assessment is self-discrediting in the described poorly perfused wound.
Another postponement cue substitutes for a credible coordinated care plan.

fairness: Urgent surgical and vascular assessment is defensible for concurrent infection and severe perfusion impairment; maintained blood pressure does not remove limb urgency.
Combining two stated problems into the only combined response does not establish two consequential inferences. This is important but easy safety content.
The retrospective task and presentation are coherent and self-contained.
suggestions: Compare credible coordinated plans, retaining urgent findings, instead of urgent assessment against unsupported delay.
For a sequencing question, provide facts that distinguish the plans and obtain clinician review; do not invent a universal drainage/revascularization order.
Alternatively seek explicit acceptance of a foundational safety-recognition role.

title: Foot scan review - neuropathic change and infection
clarityIssues: Resolve the diagnosis should distinguish histological assessment from pathogen identification; the requested analyses are unspecified.

cues.phrase: states that superimposed infection cannot be resolved
cues.why: The report supplies the diagnostic limitation the learner would otherwise interpret, leaving a direct sampling question.
The named treatment compartment matches only the bone specimen.

cues.phrase: Aseptic bone specimen from the involved midfoot
cues.why: Only this option advertises asepsis and explicitly targets the involved compartment.

fairness: A representative bone specimen is defensible for consequential uncertainty about osteomyelitis with neuropathic change. Surface culture does not resolve that distinction.
The explanation reasonably notes MRI specificity limits, but the stem gives that interpretation. Diagnostic certainty should not be promised from unspecified specimen analysis.
The standalone case is coherent; no hidden prior findings are needed.
suggestions: Clarify whether histology and culture are sought and phrase collection quality consistently.
Use a consequential interpretation of discordant findings or sampling without hiding genuine radiologist uncertainty.
Avoid duplicating the preceding bone-sampling item with an explicitly supplied MRI limitation.

title: Hospital infection review - initial exploration
fairness: Progression during treatment, deep symptoms beyond erythema and fascial fluid support urgent exploration despite absent gas, a low laboratory score and maintained blood pressure.
The learner weighs conflicting evidence, then selects action over imaging or observation. MRI and monitored treatment are credible errors from overreliance on reassuring findings.
The explanation appropriately says negative findings do not reliably exclude necrotizing infection; it does not claim every fascial-fluid finding proves necrosis.
Subsequent operative and wound updates are coherent. This offline editorial PASS is not clinical approval or fresh guideline verification.
suggestions: For precision in a future version, name the laboratory instrument instead of laboratory risk score; no invented numeric cutoff is needed.

title: Hospital infection review - return to theatre
clarityIssues: Continue bedside dressings before the next operation leaves timing unspecified and could describe interim care while urgent return is arranged.

cues.why: Closure of a newly discolored, increasingly tender wound is an obviously premature endpoint.

cues.phrase: new discoloration and tenderness extending past the previously viable edge
cues.why: Directly signals progression, while alternatives offer closure or vague delay rather than competing responses.

fairness: Prompt operative reassessment/debridement is defensible for new local progression; systemic improvement does not establish local control.
The sequence is coherent and the update supplies the earlier operation. Prior feedback already taught progression despite reassuring findings, so this largely repeats the rule.
Bedside dressing care is not mutually exclusive with operative return unless the intended delay is specified.
suggestions: State the actual decision timing without inventing a fixed interval.
Use plausible same-stage responses instead of closure and ambiguous interim care, or seek a basic reassessment exception.

title: Hospital infection review - tissue preservation
clarityIssues: Resect the diseased fascia is less explicit than removal of all involved nonviable tissue. Preservation must remain conditional on adequate debridement and demonstrable viability.

cues.phrase: could expose the involved fascia while retaining perfused overlying skin
cues.why: This feasibility permission directly supplies the reason for skin preservation.

cues.phrase: Neighboring muscle contracted and bled when assessed.
cues.why: Together with the skin-preservation permission, this protects both extra tissues named only in the radical-resection distractor; the remaining option drains rather than resects.

fairness: Preserving demonstrably viable tissue while adequately removing involved nonviable tissue is defensible; no confident clinical error in that principle is identified.
The wording could overteach fascia-only resection as a fixed operation. Exact extent and skin preservation need clinician review of the operative findings.
The update follows re-exploration coherently and stands alone, but the author supplies both tissue eligibility and access.
suggestions: Remove feasibility permission and retain necessary operative observations.
Express complete removal of involved nonviable tissue with reassessment of retained tissue, rather than an unconditional layer-only rule.
Compare credible extents of debridement and have a clinician confirm that the observations uniquely rank them.

title: Persistent axillary drainage - residual-disease planning
clarityIssues: Tunnel-procedure assessment does not name a concrete procedure or receiving specialty.

cues.phrase: one superficial channel without a separate tense cavity
cues.why: Channel maps to the tunnel choice, while the negative directly eliminates abscess drainage.

cues.phrase: New tender nodules have become uncommon
cues.why: With the structural-channel wording this downranks medical escalation, leaving the tunnel-specific referral.

fairness: A persistent localized draining tunnel after inflammatory improvement reasonably supports procedural assessment, alongside ongoing medical care.
Broad category choices and supplied discriminators make this one decision, not two consequential steps.
The later deroofing node repeats the same anatomy and response; the pair rehearses the same discriminator.
suggestions: Name a concrete assessment/referral plan and specify the genuine remaining medical-versus-procedural decision.
Combine this with deroofing or give the later node a genuinely different consequential finding.

title: Persistent axillary drainage - localized procedure
clarityIssues: Which procedure may be offered is permissive rather than clearly asking for the best next procedure.

cues.why: Matches the limited option after the prior node establishes a tunnel-directed procedure.

cues.phrase: There is no confluent scarred field or separate tense abscess.
cues.why: The two negatives correspond directly to regional excision and incision/drainage.

cues.phrase: that residual problem merits procedural assessment within ongoing HS care
cues.why: Prior feedback has resolved the structural-versus-inflammatory distinction; the update adds no substantial new discriminator.

fairness: Deroofing is a reasonable best offered procedure for a recurrent superficial tunnel. Regional excision is not necessarily impossible to offer, making the permissive task insufficiently precise.
The chronology and current anatomy are clear, but deleting the update leaves essentially the same choice from the initial presentation.
This is one-rule matching, especially after the referral feedback.
suggestions: Ask for the best next procedure and verify the ranking against a genuinely close alternative.
Replace repeated extent/absence facts with a new planning consequence, or merge the nodes.
Retain necessary abscess exclusion without listing a verbatim disqualification of every competitor.

title: Axillary movement pain - extensive disease
clarityIssues: Expand HS as hidradenitis suppurativa on first use for a self-contained case.

cues.phrase: throughout that field rather than one isolated channel
cues.why: Explicitly contrasts broad-field treatment with limited deroofing and announces the extent decision.
The only broad definitive procedure matches the broad scarred field; acute drainage has no supporting collection.

fairness: Regional excision is a reasonable discussion for extensive chronic tunnels and functional impairment; this does not prove every other tunnel procedure is impossible.
This high-yield indication is currently a single extent-matching rule, with distribution interpreted for the learner.
New-site disease in the later update is coherent and does not change this local decision.
suggestions: Show the observed map and functional restriction without the explicit rather-than comparison.
Compare credible procedures for this extent, with a patient-specific discriminator; avoid acute drainage as filler.
Expand the diagnosis abbreviation once.

title: Axillary movement pain - new sites after surgery
clarityIssues: New tender nodules lack recurrence, extent, treatment and examination details needed for a meaningful medical-versus-procedural decision.

cues.why: Repeats the already stated absence of drainage and improvement, eliminating re-exploration.

cues.phrase: Surgical re-exploration of the healed axilla
cues.why: Explicitly targets the healed site instead of the symptomatic sites.

cues.phrase: Dermatology consultation for the newly active regions
cues.why: The only assessment before treatment competes with immediate regional excision of unspecified new nodules.

fairness: Dermatology assessment is reasonable, but wins through wrong-site and premature-treatment errors rather than a close resident decision.
The postoperative chronology is coherent and the update stands alone. Recognizing disease at other sites is not two consequential steps.
Feedback should not imply all new-site lesions require exclusively medical treatment; assessment determines subsequent care.
suggestions: Replace the wrong-site alternative with plans for the actual lesions at the same decision stage.
Supply pattern and treatment facts that distinguish medical escalation, local procedure and assessment.
Do not manufacture complexity merely to teach that local surgery does not cure disease elsewhere.

title: Axillary care review - acute collection
clarityIssues: Expand HS in the standalone visible case.

cues.why: Supplies the immediate target; drainage competes only with broad chronic excision or deferral.

cues.phrase: chronic-disease procedural appointment was already planned for later
cues.why: Overtly divides acute drainage now from chronic planning later, giving the sequencing rule before the choice.

fairness: Incision and drainage can provide acute relief of a tense painful HS abscess; it is not definitive treatment of chronic tunnels.
Acute versus chronic care is high yield, but the alternatives make this one-step source-control recognition.
The outside-record frame is coherent and specifies the time point.
suggestions: Expand the diagnosis and retain the pain/function findings.
Compare plausible immediate procedures or a supported consequential treatment-stage boundary; otherwise seek a basic acute-relief exception.
Keep longitudinal limitations in feedback instead of presenting the complete acute/chronic rule beforehand.

title: Painful cleft swelling - acute drainage

cues.why: The key echoes the tense/fluctuant swelling, while the pit procedure labels itself elective.
Elective is a self-disqualifying stage qualifier in a task about current acute swelling.

fairness: Incision and drainage is the defensible best offered treatment for acute pilonidal abscess. Above-anus location is legitimate diagnostic context.
The chronic history adds no second consequential decision against plainly elective definitive procedures.
Later resolution and persistent drainage are coherent; the feedback previews a chronic decision but does not name its exact procedure.
suggestions: Use neutral parallel procedure labels without elective only in a distractor.
Make a real competing procedural/anatomical issue determine immediate care, or obtain explicit foundational-role acceptance.

title: Painful cleft swelling - persistent chronic disease
clarityIssues: Which referral plan does not match Continue cleft hygiene and dressing care, which is not a referral.
The old midline scar and prior pit-directed treatment first appear in the update; identify these clearly as prior treatment history.

cues.why: Grammatically filters out conservative care before clinical reasoning.

cues.phrase: No acute cavity is found at reassessment.
cues.why: Directly eliminates repeat abscess drainage, the only alternative procedure.
With failed prior treatment, this leaves the sole escalation/referral choice against unchanged care.

fairness: Excisional assessment is reasonable for symptomatic recurrent interconnected disease after a limited procedure; it does not establish one mandatory operation.
The update clearly separates resolved acute swelling from chronic drainage and stands alone, but the choices create a simple escalation rule.
Previous feedback already announces a separate chronic decision; the follow-up needs a real remaining comparison.
suggestions: Use a neutral management task or make every option a referral.
Compare credible elective strategies instead of drainage without an abscess and unchanged conservative care.
Clarify treatment chronology without adding unnecessary history.

title: Painful cleft swelling - closure strategy
clarityIssues: The initial presentation still describes a tense abscess. State its resolution in this later update so closure remains unambiguous without the preceding node.
The reconstructive discussion compares wound strategies rather than requiring one named flap is author-facing instruction, not a clinical observation.

cues.why: Failed beside a midline-closure option encourages avoidance by wording; the actual procedure and recurrence should establish the history.

fairness: Off-midline closure is defensible when excision/closure are appropriate. Avoiding prolonged open-wound care is a legitimate patient constraint, not a fact to remove merely because it affects the answer.
Two consequential selections are possible: use care constraints to choose closure over open healing, then select the closure strategy for recurrent disease.
The full sequence resolves the acute episode, but the latest update alone does not say so. Closed wounds must not be portrayed as guaranteeing no wound-care burden.
suggestions: State that the acute collection has resolved and describe prior treatment rather than only calling the scar failed.
Remove the meta-instruction about named flaps.
Keep the care constraint and parallel strategies, distinguishing planned closure from guaranteed uncomplicated healing.

title: Low cleft drainage - establish the source

cues.why: Only the anorectal examination addresses the named location; imaging deliberately targets the other site.

cues.phrase: Ultrasound confined to the upper pits
cues.why: Confined advertises that the choice does not assess the draining opening.

fairness: Anorectal examination including anoscopy is a reasonable initial assessment for a potentially anorectal source; upper pits do not prove the source.
The differential is important, but the options reduce it to symptomatic-site matching rather than two consequential steps.
The standalone presentation and task are coherent. Anoscopy must not be presented as guaranteed to delineate every fistula.
suggestions: Compare assessments that plausibly evaluate the actual opening and source, with facts distinguishing their sequence.
Keep uncertainty about the upper-pit connection and remove the deliberately wrong-site restriction.
Explain why anorectal assessment is needed without promising definitive fistula mapping.

title: Painful back lump - acute procedure
clarityIssues: New tension and pain are stated, but not erythema, warmth or another explicit inflammatory examination change. The later node says redness resolved although redness was never described.
fairness: Recognizing an epidermoid-type lesion and distinguishing its acute inflammatory/collection phase from elective capsule removal can be consequential steps.

A debris-containing cavity also describes cyst contents. Pain/tension support inflammation, but the examination is less decisive for drainage over immediate excision than the explanation implies. This is clinical sufficiency uncertainty, not a confident assertion that the key is wrong.
Return to a quiet symptomatic nodule is plausible, but unexplained redness and pre-announced removal weaken chronology and later independent difficulty.
suggestions: Add a concise supported observation establishing the acute inflammatory/drainable phase; do not equate ultrasound debris with infection.
Explain why immediate excision is less appropriate for this exact presentation after the answer.
Remove the next elective-removal answer from preceding feedback if a separate follow-up decision is retained.

title: Painful back lump - definitive procedure
clarityIssues: Redness and tenderness have resolved introduces antecedent redness absent from the original presentation.

cues.phrase: elective removal can be reconsidered after the inflammation settles
cues.why: Prior feedback announces the next answer; the update then states its condition has occurred.
Explicitly removes the rationale for both drainage and aspiration, leaving excision.
Repeats the elective-removal framing already taught by preceding feedback.

fairness: Elective excision is reasonable for a persistently symptomatic epidermoid-type lesion after acute inflammation resolves.
The update otherwise stands alone and follows a plausible course. Harness irritation gives a treatment indication, but neither alternative addresses the nonfluid nodule.
This is a rehearsed one-rule follow-up, not an independent two-step resident decision.
suggestions: Remove the next answer from prior feedback and correct the inflammation chronology.
Compare plausible elective choices using a supported patient-specific discriminator.
If routine excision versus aspiration/drainage is retained, seek foundational-role acceptance rather than claiming moderate/hard reasoning.
